annotations.annotation_text: Page 68 opens Book 1, Chapter 3 ("The Trial of HCE") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues the public trial and persecution of HCE, the ballad of Hosty, and the testimony of witnesses, featuring HCE, the Twelve Jurors, Hosty. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mamalujo signal "leinster" on page 68 ("The Trial of HCE"): the Four Old Men — Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; Ulster, Munster, Leinster, Connaught — serve here as senile chroniclers and bedpost witnesses during the public trial and persecution of HCE, the ballad of Hosty, and the testimony of witnesses. In this Age of Gods passage, they observe and record the dream's events as squawking gulls circling overhead.
sources: O'Donovan, John. The Annals of the Four Masters. https://celt.ucc.ie/published/T100005A/
MacCabe, Colin. James Joyce and the Revolution of the Word. https://archive.org/details/jamesjoycerevolu0000macc

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 68 ("The Trial of HCE"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
